scope: exhaustive occurrence histograms for every bit pattern at each actual input length
status: analytical extrapolation; no 5--10 B B300 run was executed

baseline.implementation: specialized exact-length model; no compressed stream materialization

scenarios.constant_4B_throughput: Optimistic sensitivity: every longer input retains the measured 4 B inputs/s.
scenarios.quadratic_per_input_cost: Planning estimate: per-input kernel work scales with (input_bytes / 4)^2.
scenarios.cubic_per_input_cost: Conservative sensitivity: per-input kernel work scales with (input_bytes / 4)^3.

implementation_requirements: The current CUDA implementation is specialized to 1--4 B and must be extended and revalidated.
Five through seven bytes fit a uint64 population counter.
Eight bytes has exactly 2^64 inputs and therefore requires prefix sharding instead of one uint64 population value.
Eight through ten bytes need wider host-side total and occurrence aggregation; nine and ten byte populations exceed 2^64.
Longer fixed arrays and additional per-input work may change register pressure, occupancy, atomics and throughput.
limitations: The three scenarios are sensitivity calculations, not measurements, confidence intervals, or mathematical bounds.
Kernel time excludes scheduler queueing, allocation, container conversion, CUDA startup, host transfer, validation and publication.
Exact CPU agreement is established only for the measured 1--4 B implementations.
A 5--10 B implementation must be independently checked against libbzip2 fixtures before its histogram is trusted.
